dialogue.opening_line: I keep coughing when I drink. Am I meant to just carry on?

action_responses.introduce_and_permission: Yes, please. I want to know what is going on.
action_responses.clarify_difficulty: It is drinks. I cough, and my voice sounds wet afterwards.
action_responses.check_wellbeing: I am comfortable now. I am not short of breath.
action_responses.explain_scope: All right. So you are not guessing—you are getting your supervisor.
action_responses.pause_and_escalate: I will leave the drink there while you contact them.
action_responses.teach_back_plan: I will not drink for now, and I will wait here for the supervising SLT.
action_responses.factual_handover: Thank you for telling them exactly what I said.

fallback_responses: I want someone to explain it clearly.
I have not tried another drink since I told you.

facts.fact: Jordan reports coughing with drinks and a wet-sounding voice afterwards.
Jordan is comfortable at rest in this authored scenario.
The supervising SLT has acknowledged the escalation.

dialogue.opening_line: Mum says talking in class is hard... but I like drawing.

action_responses.welcome_and_assent: Okay. I want to start with drawing.
action_responses.explain_session: Drawing, then talking, then I can have a break.
action_responses.child_led_observation: This is our playground. The big tree is where we play hide-and-seek.
action_responses.gather_parent_view: Mum: Busy group work and long instructions are difficult. Leah nods.
action_responses.gather_child_view: When everyone talks fast, I cannot get my turn.
action_responses.processing_support: That is easier. One thing, then I can answer.
action_responses.shared_summary: Yes. Talking fast is the hard bit—not all talking.
action_responses.agree_next_step: A movement break first, then we can do the next activity.

fallback_responses: I want a little break first.

facts.fact: Leah uses longer descriptions during an unhurried drawing interaction.
Busy group work and multi-step instructions are reported as difficult.
Leah finds it hard to take a turn when classmates talk quickly.

dialogue.opening_line: By the last lesson my voice feels finished. I need something that fits real teaching.

action_responses.contract_session: Yes. I want to focus on getting through a teaching day.
action_responses.explore_impact: It is most effortful after lunch, and I stop joining staff conversations.
action_responses.elicit_client_theory: Noise and talking over the class make it harder, but I do not think it is simply bad habits.
action_responses.explain_boundaries: Good. I would rather be properly assessed than given a quick label.
action_responses.set_shared_goal: A realistic goal is finishing the final lesson with enough voice for the instructions.
action_responses.agree_monitoring: I can note effort before and after the final lesson without judging myself.
action_responses.summarise_plan: Yes—that is my goal, and the next step is a fuller supervised assessment.

fallback_responses: How would that work in my classroom?
I do not want this to become a list of things I have done wrong.
That sounds closer to what matters to me.

facts.fact: Voice effort is greatest after lunch and reduces Aisha's staff-room participation.
Aisha does not want the concern framed as personal failure or bad habits.
Aisha's chosen goal is to finish the final lesson with enough voice for classroom instructions.
